correctness.rationale: For traceless matrices polarizing X²=Q(X)I yields XY+YX=B(X,Y)I and ad_X²Y=4Q(X)Y−2B(X,Y)X. For X=0, nonzero isotropic X, and nonisotropic X the ranks are 0, 1, 2 with Y-fiber sizes q³, q², q respectively; the nonzero images are the line through X or X⊥ as asserted. For Z=0, W=0 necessarily; the total is q³+(q²−1)q²+(q³−q²)q=2q⁴−q². For nonzero nilpotent Z conjugate to E₁₂, X⊥Z means X is upper triangular, and [X,Z]=2aZ for diagonal a,−a. Nonzero isotropic X forcing Z lies on its line and gives W=0; each prescribed nonzero multiple fixes a and leaves q choices of the other coordinate. For Q(Z)≠0, ad_Z on Z⊥ squares to 4Q(Z) and therefore fixes the candidate X=−[Z,W]/(4Q(Z)) uniquely for W⊥Z. The determinant of 2ZW−B(Z,W)I gives Q([Z,W])=B(Z,W)²−4Q(Z)Q(W), proving the nonisotropy test. The equation a²+bc=s has q(q−1)+q times the number of square roots of s solutions, with the q(q−1) term added only once. For Q(Z) square, Z is diagonalizable and Z⊥ is the off-diagonal split plane; in the nonsquare case a nonzero isotropic vector in Z⊥ would make Z triangular after conjugation, which is impossible. These counts give the stated support and the conditional laws. All arguments use odd characteristic, labeled inputs, and no quotient by conjugacy for counting. The bundled verify_joint.py and verify_joint_output.txt were inspected, not rerun; the recorded support values for q=3,5,7,9 agree with the analytic count. VERIFICATION.md does not supply independent attestation or formal checking.
